claim: The stack=0 step-face reader lines_step_load still reads the pre-V5 3-byte slot layout (lower face at bytes 3-5) while the only writer, ts_step_faces via ts_piece_wr, unconditionally stores 4-byte pieces with the lower piece at byte 8 (line 1795), so the writer and reader disagree on the slot layout with no shared constant.
scenario: Build with steps=True, stack_steps=False (permitted: wall_renderer.py:254 asserts only stack=>steps, not steps=>stack). ts_step_faces records a stair riser as [y1][y2][cls][bpid] at byte 8; the rep(steps*(1-stack)) call at line 2568 makes lines_step_load read bytes 3-5, i.e. the upper piece's bpid byte as ly1 and two never-written u2-slot bytes as ly2p1/lcol -> every lower step face (stair riser) vanishes or emits a garbage 1-row run, diverging from the oracle. Evades certification because all gated builds since V5 run stack=1; this reader is only instantiated in non-certified knob builds.
v_reason: Verified in the working tree: ts_piece_wr (frame_render.fj:1551) always writes 4-byte pieces with the lower piece at slot byte 8 (call at line 1795), unconditionally on stack — there is no 3-byte writer left. lines_step_load (line 2075) reads upper at bytes 0-2 and lower at bytes 3-5 (lines 2110-2135); it was half-migrated to V5 (16-byte stride at line 2104, count-nibble flags) but kept the pre-V5 intra-slot offsets, so lower faces read the upper piece's bpid as ly1 and two never-written u2-slot bytes as ly2p1/lcol. Upper faces survive only by coincidence ([y1][y2][cls] prefix matches). wall_renderer.py:254 permits steps=True/stack_steps=False (default False), and rep(steps*(1-stack)) at line 2568 instantiates the broken reader in exactly that config, while the oracle's stack_steps=False path paints real lower faces (reference_model.py:1941-1944) — guaranteed divergence. Evades certification because all gated builds pass stack_steps=True (deg_gate.py:38, ba25_sheet.py:34, bshare25.py:58), where lines_step_load is never emitted and the stack reader lines_steps_load2 uses the correct layout. R6 violation (no shared layout constant between writer and reader); latent defect in a reachable permitted configuration, worth fixing now.

claim: project_thing converts istep to downscaled texels with `rep(ds/2, k) hex.shr_bit 8, istepo`, i.e. division by 2^(ds/2), which equals the oracle's `istep // self.downscale` (reference_model.project_thing, line ~1199) only for ds in {1,2,4} — the formula should be log2(ds) shifts, so any other TEXTURE_DOWNSCALE silently drifts from the oracle.
scenario: cfg.TEXTURE_DOWNSCALE = max(1, 320 // W) (config.py:41). Build at W=40 -> ds=8 -> fj shifts istepo right 4 bits (divide by 16) while the oracle divides by 8; every sprite's vertical DDA step is halved, sprites render stretched to double texel height and the byte-exact gate fails on any frame with a visible thing. Evades current certification because all gates and the 260-frame sweep run only the W=160 (ds=2) config, where 2^(ds/2)==ds coincidentally holds.
v_reason: Confirmed at src/fj/projection.fj:1575 (new in this branch). hex.shr_bit is a one-bit shift (verified in flipjump stl shifts.fj:17), so `rep(ds/2, k) hex.shr_bit 8, istepo` divides by 2^(ds/2), while the oracle (reference_model.py:1198) divides istep by ds; the two agree only for ds in {1,2,4}. ds is cfg.TEXTURE_DOWNSCALE = max(1, 320//W) (config.py:45), passed via wall_renderer.py:1308 -> thing_record_body -> project_thing, so W=40 gives ds=8: fj shifts 4 bits (/16) vs oracle /8, halving every sprite's vertical DDA step and breaking byte-exactness on any frame with a visible thing. All gates and the 260-frame sweep run only W=160 (ds=2), where the coincidence holds, so certification cannot see it. R6 violation is corroborated by the sibling wall path in the same file (column_setup, projection.fj:1270) which does the same downscale with a general hex.div by ds — the correct fix (a shift-count of log2(ds) still fails non-power-of-two ds like W=64 -> ds=5, which the config formula can produce). Latent defect worth fixing now: replace the shifts with the existing hex.div-by-ds pattern (or statically assert ds in {1,2,4} at emit time).

claim: wedge_qt (and wedge_bbox_plane at line 557) evaluate the half-plane quantity Q on 4-nibble high slices, so the byte-exact wedge cull is only correct while every true Q — including the dx+dy / dy-dx combinations for Q1/Q3 — fits signed 16 bits, an invariant that holds for E1M1's ~5440-unit extent but not for arbitrary int16 DOOM maps, while the paired oracle (mapcompiler.bbox_wedge_miss, exact Python ints) never wraps; the bbox_wedge_miss docstring's "|Q| < 2^15 for int16 maps" overstates the guarantee (int16 coords give |dx+dy| up to ~131070).
scenario: Bake a map (or thing-inflated bbox) whose corner-to-eye deltas satisfy e.g. dx=20000, dy=15000 for the Q3 plane: true Q=35000 (inside), but mod-16^4 two's-complement reads 35000-65536=-30536 -> nibble-3 sign negative -> corner classified outside -> wedge_bbox rejects a visible subtree and whole rooms of walls vanish, while the oracle keeps them (parity break). Invisible to all current certification because only E1M1 is ever baked; surfaces the first time a larger-extent map is compiled.
v_reason: Verified in the working tree: wedge_qt (projection.fj:506, Q arithmetic at 518-534) and wedge_bbox_plane (:557, 578-593) evaluate Q on 4-nibble high slices and classify via hex.sign 4/hex.if0 4, so the result is true-Q mod 2^16 read as signed 16-bit — correct only while |Q| < 2^15. Q1/Q3 are dy-dx / dx+dy (up to ~±131070 for int16 coords), so the invariant is not implied by int16 maps, and the paired oracle (mapcompiler.bbox_wedge_miss:116-130, exact Python ints, consumed by reference_model.bsp_render_order:645-649) never wraps — a structural R6 parity break in the unsafe direction (fj rejects a visible subtree the oracle keeps; walls vanish). The bbox_wedge_miss docstring's "|Q| < 2^15 for int16 maps" (line 121) overstates the guarantee exactly as claimed. No bake-time guard enforces the bound (only encode_fixed_point range-checks the seg affine c), so a larger-extent map bakes silently. Certification evasion is valid: only E1M1 (~5440-unit extent, all |Q| well under 2^15) is ever baked, so the 7-gate + 260-frame byte-exact sweeps cannot see it. Latent, not shipped-behavior-breaking, but worth fixing now via a cheap bake-time extent assert (precedent exists) plus docstring correction.

Safe today (max 120 of 255) but the constraint is invisible at the definition site and unchecked at the Python emit site; same pattern at the bottom-list compare a few lines below (line 665).

Latent R6-class defect; the fix is a one-line Python assert (5*TS_ECAP <= 255) at the SSOT definition site, worth adding now.

claim: recip32 implements only the right-normalize path of the shared block-FP reciprocal, so for 0 < planeheight < 0x100 it indexes slopediv_recip's unpopulated zero region (step=0), whereas the shipped oracle _recip_div32 (reference_model.py:358-361) has a left-normalize branch and computes a true reciprocal -- a genuine fj-vs-oracle parity divergence, not the shared limitation the line-14 scope comment ('matching how M13pS2a's oracle prototype also only validated realistic magnitudes') implies.
scenario: A nonzero planeheight in [1, 0xFF] (under ~0.004 world units) makes fj's step 0: the ascending walk sees ys >= threshold_hi (=0) every row and slams zidx to 127, the descending walk never moves -- while the oracle's _zidx_band_walk computes correct bands, so the frames diverge byte-for-byte. Unreachable in certification because every real E1M1 planeheight is |integer_sector_height<<16 - integer_viewz<<16|, i.e. 0 or a multiple of 0x10000; any future fractional viewz (bobbing, interpolation) or fractional plane heights would open the gap.
v_reason: Verified in code: recip32 (src/fj/plane_bands.fj:23-30) only right-normalizes (shifts while sph>0xFFF), so for planeheight in [1,0xFF] it indexes slopediv_recip below 0x100, which tables.py:201-204 explicitly leaves zero ("m<0x100 unused -> 0"), yielding step=0 — ascending walk then slams zidx to 127 (ys>=thi6=0 always bumps), descending never moves. The shipped oracle _recip_div32 (reference_model.py:354-361) has the left-normalize P<2 branch producing a true reciprocal, and _zidx_band_walk (line 1336) consumes it for any nonzero planeheight, so fj and oracle genuinely diverge on this domain (they are provably identical for divisor>=0x100, which I also checked). Certification evasion holds: bb_ph is computed at runtime (frame_render.fj:813-820) as |int_height<<16 - viewz| with integer viewz at every gate, so certified planeheights are always 0 or multiples of 0x10000; fractional viewz (M14 bobbing/interpolation, the declared next milestone) opens the window whenever the eye passes within ~0.004 units of a plane height. The line-14 comment's claim that the oracle "also only validated realistic magnitudes" conflates the pS2a prototype with the shipped oracle, which handles the range — this is a real R6 latent parity defect, cheap to fix (add the left-normalize branch or clamp bb_ph), not a shared scope limit. build_bands_bs shares the same leaf and the same gap.

claim: v5_side_modes suppresses double-sky pieces only for the lip case (um == 2), not the riser case (um == 1), so an upper step-face band is drawn floating in the sky between two F_SKY1 ceilings of differing heights — violating the code's own V2 rule quoted three lines above ('nothing may draw lines in the sky').
scenario: E1M1 (assets/doom1.wad) has 8 such linedefs (130-132: sky ceilings 264 vs 128; 250-254: 216 vs 24/64 — the outdoor courtyard/nukage boundaries; verified by direct WAD scan). Viewed from the higher-ceiling side with the shipped config (sky=True, near_steps=True), um_==1 passes the face gate, and _face_paint fills the rows between the two sky-ceiling projections with STEP_FACE_BASE gray inside the ceiling region where the sky was just painted — a tall gray slab hanging in the sky whenever one of these boundaries lands in the STEP_SEG_BUDGET=8 nearest face-carrying segs. This evades the byte-exact certification because oracle and fj share this SSOT: the 7-viewpoint gates and the 260-frame sweep prove oracle==fj equality, not look-correctness, and the gate viewpoints evidently never put one of these 8 boundaries into the face budget. Fix shape: suppress um for ANY um != 0 when both ceil_texes are F_SKY1 (DOOM's double-sky hack draws no upper wall there at all).
v_reason: Verified against the code and the WAD. v5_side_modes (reference_model.py:947) suppresses double-sky pieces only for um==2 (lip); um==1 (front ceiling higher) passes through, and the consumer (lines 1634-1706, painted at 1931-1940 via _face_paint, which has no sky check) fills rows between the two sky-ceiling projections with STEP_FACE_BASE gray inside the ceiling region that _render_planes_flat just painted as sky (line 2265) — with stack_steps, _region_paint (line 1913) paints sky again below the face, so the slab floats between sky above and below. Direct scan of assets/doom1.wad E1M1 confirms exactly 8 such linedefs: 130-132 (ceil 264 vs 128) and 250-254 (216 vs 24/64, 24 vs 64), each with a um==1 side. The certification-evasion story is sound: fj (wall_renderer.py:798,1861) calls the same v5_side_modes SSOT, so byte-exact oracle==fj gates prove equality, not look-correctness. Vanilla DOOM's double-sky hack draws no upper wall there at all; the fix (suppress any um != 0 when both ceil_texes are F_SKY1) matches both DOOM and the function's own documented V2 rule three lines above, so this is a missed case, not a design choice.

claim: _scale_recip_div hangs in an infinite loop ('while sden < 0x100: sden <<= 4' never terminates from 0) instead of failing loudly when den_abs == 0 (or negative), and it is the shared SSOT reciprocal kernel called from three subsystems (wall scale, sprite projection/istep, sprite_tz_min_size).
scenario: Every current call site happens to guard (scale_from_global_angle pre-checks den == 0; project_thing guarantees tz >= SPRITE_MINZ and xscale >= 2^16/wph before the istep call), so shipped behavior is unaffected — but a future caller passing an unclamped or wrapped-negative divisor (e.g. M14 sim work reusing the kernel, or an experiment relaxing SPRITE_MINZ) freezes the oracle mid-render with no traceback, which is far harder to diagnose than a raised error. A one-line 'assert den_abs > 0' preserves all certified behavior.
v_reason: Verified in src/doomfj/reference_model.py:447-449: with den_abs == 0 the normalization loop 'while sden < 0x100: sden <<= 4' spins forever (0<<4==0), and a negative den_abs also never terminates — a silent hang with no traceback. The function is the self-documented SSOT mirror of the fj proj.scale_recip_div macro and is called from all three claimed subsystems (wall scale line 476, sprite xscale/istep lines 1167/1198, sprite_tz_min_size h_at line 1036, which the emitter bakes sp_tzmax from). Every current call site is guarded (den==0 early-return at line 471; tz >= SPRITE_MINZ=4<<16 at line 1162; xscale==0 implies h==0 rejected by h<min_h at line 1182 before the istep call; h_at's search domain starts at SPRITE_MINZ), so shipped byte-exact certification is unaffected — the hazard is strictly latent, triggerable only by a future caller (e.g. M14 sim reuse, which the roadmap names as next). A guard raising on den_abs <= 0 is provably behavior-preserving on all certified paths and converts an undiagnosable freeze into an immediate error; worth adding now. Minor corrections to the claim: R6 is a stretch as the rule tag (nothing duplicated — "none" fits better), and prefer an explicit raise over a bare assert since python -O strips asserts.

claim: The degrade-package merge uses `or` (deg_sliver = deg_sliver or DEG_SLIVER_W, etc., lines 1408-1413), so an explicitly passed 0 is indistinguishable from 'not passed' and is silently replaced by the certified default — the comment at line 1406 ('any explicit value wins') is false for the disable value 0, which is exactly the value these knobs use to mean OFF elsewhere (e.g. `deg_stack_scale == 0` at the gate sites).

No current caller hits it (all scratchpad ablations use the additive degrade=False direction; all degrade=True calls pass no overrides), which is precisely the certification-evasion story — latent for future research invocations, no shipped-pixel impact. Repo shipping decisions are driven by these lever attributions, so the trivial None-sentinel fix is worth making now.

claim: lines_pid is nowhere asserted to fit its storage: the two_sided branch bakes ("seg_pid", 4, ...) into a register declared `seg_pid: hex.vec 2` (line 1775, with `vzbank` immediately after it), the shipped plane_near tier bakes it at 2 nibbles (line 929), and the per-column attribution store `pclm` (line 1417) holds one byte per column -- yet unlike every other bank in this file (step classes, sprite light classes, sprite blocks `blk < 0x10000`, WPX stride) there is no `len(lines_pid) <= 255` assert.

On a future map (M15 multi-level is the stated roadmap) with >255 distinct (ceil,floor) key pairs, pid 256+ is silently truncated: the shipped tier's one-byte pclm write aliases two different plane pairs (columns attributed to the wrong sector's floor/ceiling band lists -> wrong colours), and in the two_sided lab build the width-4 `hex.xor_by 4, seg_pid` flips nibbles 2-3, which belong to `vzbank` -- corrupting the frame's band-bank pointer. No build-time error either way; a one-line assert at the registration site (line 566) catches it.
v_reason: Every detail verified in the working tree: lines_pid (wall_renderer.py:546, registered at 565-577) has no width assert, unlike the file's own convention (asserts at 1717, 1866, 1960, 1992). All runtime consumers are byte-wide — seg_pid declared hex.vec 2 at line 1775 with vzbank immediately after (1776), pclm is one byte per column (frame_render.fj:1180, written via hex.write_byte at 1925/2313/2335), and lines_pid_addrs/lines_pid_ids read only 2 nibbles (frame_render.fj:1959, 1973). The shipped plane_near tier bakes pid at width 2 (line 929) so pid>=256 silently aliases mod 256 (wrong band lists per column); the two_sided lab build bakes width 4 (line 895) into the 2-nibble register, so a pid>=256 constant would flip nibbles belonging to vzbank during the SET..USE window of the xor-involution, corrupting the frame's bank pointer while pass-2 runs. Neither path errors at build time (stl width-N constant macros use only the low 4N bits). Certification is unaffected because E1M1 has ~113 plane pairs (2*113=~227 unshared keys per the line-559 comment), well under 255 — the defect is latent for future maps (M15 multi-level is the stated roadmap). A one-line assert at the registration site (lines 566/577) is the fix, matching the file's existing pattern.

claim: The bbox wedge cull's width contract is wrong and unenforced: the docstring asserts |Q| < 2^15 'for int16 maps', but Q = dx+dy (corner minus view, both int16, plus the +/-96 thing inflation) can reach ~2^17 on a large map, and the fj side (wedge_bbox_plane's 4-nibble Q slices, plus wall_renderer.py:1062 staging inflated corners as (coord<<16)&0xFFFFFFFF) wraps at 2^15/int16 while this Python SSOT computes exact ints — bbox_gate_boxes has no assert guarding either bound.
scenario: Re-node a map whose extent sum (width+height) exceeds ~32768, or whose thing-carrying bbox corner sits within 96 units of +/-32767 so inflation pushes it past int16: the fj 4-nibble Q (or the wrapped <<16 corner constant) flips sign, the fj gate culls a subtree the oracle keeps (or vice versa), and whole rooms of walls/sprites vanish on one side only — byte-exact parity breaks. Evades the current certification because E1M1/E1M1-lite coordinates keep |Q| under ~9.5k; the trap arms silently the first time the toolchain is pointed at a bigger map (E1M2+ or a community WAD). Fix is a cheap bake-time assert in bbox_gate_boxes over map extents + inflated corners.
v_reason: Verified against the code: (1) mapcompiler.py:121-122 does assert "|Q| < 2^15 for int16 maps", which is unsound — Q3 = dx+dy of corner-minus-view int16 differences can reach ~2^17; the true bound is extent-based (width+height+2*96 < 2^15). (2) The fj gate is genuinely 16-bit: wedge_bbox_plane (src/fj/projection.fj:578-601) computes Q with hex.mov/add/sub 4 and decides via hex.sign 4 — mod-2^16 two's-complement, sign at bit 15. (3) wall_renderer.py:1062-1065 bakes corners as (coord<<16)&0xFFFFFFFF, so a thing-inflated corner past int16 (bbox_gate_boxes inflates ±96 with no clamp, mapcompiler.py:177) gets a sign-flipped high half. (4) The oracle consumes exact-int bbox_wedge_miss (reference_model.py:647-648), and both sides document that gate disagreement changes which marking segs spend PNEAR budget — so a Q sign flip breaks byte-exact parity silently (subtree culled on one side only). (5) bbox_gate_boxes has no assert on extents or inflated corners; nothing else guards the bound. Certification evasion holds: gates/sweep run E1M1/E1M1-lite whose Q stays under ~9.5k; the trap arms on any larger map (M15 multi-level is on the roadmap). R6 violation as claimed; a cheap bake-time assert in bbox_gate_boxes is worth adding now to turn silent divergence into a loud bake failure.

claim: Pass-1 flattening bounds only intra-group height drift: assigning the representative's floor_h moves a member sector's floor by up to floor_tol=24 relative to NON-member neighbours, so a cross-boundary step that was exactly at DOOM's 24-unit climb limit can become 48 and block a route — the group range cap (and the 'a staircase can NEVER collapse into an unreachable cliff' comment) does not cover steps to sectors outside the group.
scenario: Sector B (floor 0) unions with C (floor 24, heavier) and takes floor 24; protected neighbour A (floor -24, tagged so never merged) previously offered a 24-unit climbable step into B — after simplify the step is 48 and the path is impassable. Harmless today (M14 movement/sim not built; renderer-only), but it silently violates the module's 'keeps its layout and play' contract the moment walking ships; a post-pass check that every surviving two-sided boundary preserves original-step<=24 => new-step<=24 would close it.
v_reason: Confirmed and empirically stronger than claimed. The group range cap (mapsimplify.py:132-137) bounds only intra-group drift; line 194's rep-floor assignment moves members up to 24 (32 via pass-3 micro-absorb tolerances) relative to non-member neighbours, and no pass or validation checks cross-boundary step passability (make_e1m1_lite.py checks floor shifts/renders only). Ran simplify on freedoom E1M1 with shipped defaults: 12 boundaries go from climbable (<=24) to blocked (>24), e.g. lines 691/694 sectors 110/118 step 16->48 and line 563 sectors 96/97 step 0->32. A DOOM-rules reachability check (up-step<=24, drops free, headroom>=56, specials open) shows lite sectors 86/88 become unreachable from the player start, stranding a sergeant (type 9) and the shotgun (2001) that are reachable in stock — violating the module's 'keeps its layout and play' contract and the 'never an unreachable cliff' comment. Evades certification because byte-exact gates compare renderer vs oracle on the SAME flattened geometry; the defect is latent for M14 movement (the declared next milestone) and is already baked into tests/fixtures/e1m1_lite.wad. Worth fixing now via a post-pass step-preservation check (original-step<=24 => new-step<=24) that vetoes the offending unions.

claim: bbox_wedge_miss's SSOT docstring claims '|Q| < 2^15 for int16 maps, matching the fj 4-nibble slice arithmetic', but Q = (cx+cy)-(vx+vy) reaches +/-131070 on maps spanning more than ~16k units, and nothing (neither bbox_gate_boxes nor proj.wedge_bbox) guards the range.
scenario: Load any map whose coordinate span exceeds ~16384 units (legal int16 WAD): the fj gate (src/fj/projection.fj wedge_bbox_plane, hex.add/sub 4 + hex.sign 4) wraps Q mod 2^16 while the Python mirror computes it exactly, so the oracle and fj disagree on the gated set and the fj build can silently cull a visible subtree — whole rooms of geometry/sprites vanish. Evades certification because E1M1/E1M1-lite spans only a few thousand units, keeping every sweep frame far below the bound; a cheap map-extent assert in bbox_gate_boxes (the SSOT choke point) would make the failure loud.
v_reason: Confirmed against the code. bbox_wedge_miss (src\doomfj\mapcompiler.py:116-130) computes Q exactly in Python, and for m&3==3, Q=(cx+cy)-(vx+vy) genuinely reaches +/-131070 on int16 coordinates, so the line-121 docstring claim "|Q| < 2^15 for int16 maps" is false as written — the real precondition is map width+height span < ~2^15 (plus the inflate=96 padding). The fj mirror (src\fj\projection.fj wedge_bbox_plane, lines 557-609) computes Q in 4-nibble (16-bit) mod-2^16 slice arithmetic and reads the sign with hex.sign 4, which misreads any |Q| >= 2^15 (no modular cancellation saves it), while the oracle gate (reference_model.py:647-648) stays exact — so on a large-span map the two sides disagree on the gated set and wedge_bbox can wrongly cull a whole visible subtree (geometry and sprites vanish). No guard exists: bbox_gate_boxes has no extent check, the only nearby assert (nodebuilder.py:231) bounds vertex count not span, and the projection.fj:381-382 "max |x|+|y| is 5440" comment is E1M1 documentation for the separate 8-nibble wexy bound, not enforcement. The certification-evasion story holds (E1M1's extent keeps every certified frame far below the bound). Latent defect worth fixing now: the roadmap plans further maps (M15 multi-level), the repo already has precedent for loud range guards (seg_affine_coeffs raises via encode_fixed_point), and a one-line map-extent assert in bbox_gate_boxes — the SSOT choke point both the oracle and the fj bake (wall_renderer.py:1054) flow through — turns a silent wrong render into a loud bake-time failure; the docstring's false "int16 maps" justification should be corrected at the same time (R6).

claim: Pass 3's micro-absorb neighbour adjacency filter (line 167) omits the impassable-flag check `(ld.flags & 1)` that pass 1's edge builder (line 148) applies, so a micro-sector can be absorbed across an impassable fence/window line that pass 1 deliberately refuses to flatten across.

Certification cannot see this: mapsimplify is an offline tool with no src/tests callers that generated tests/fixtures/e1m1_lite.wad once, and both fj and oracle render that same output. Latent defect for future maps (M15 multi-level roadmap; M14 adds the line collision that makes the invisible wall bite); the one-line fix is provably golden-neutral, hence worth fixing now.

claim: scalelight_table floors the SCREENWIDTH/viewwidth ratio before multiplying by j — `j * (DOOM_SCREENWIDTH // view_w) // DISTMAP` — which is not the DOOM formula `j*SCREENWIDTH/viewwidth/DISTMAP` the docstring itself cites as the source of truth.
scenario: At view_w=160 (and any divisor of 320) the two are identical, which is why every golden passes. But at any view width that does not divide 320 the table diverges (view_w=100, j=5: DOOM gives startmap-8, this gives startmap-7), and at view_w>320 the pre-floored ratio is 0 so wall distance-lighting silently disappears entirely. Fix `(j * DOOM_SCREENWIDTH // view_w) // DISTMAP` is byte-identical at all currently used widths.
v_reason: tables.py:85 computes `j * (DOOM_SCREENWIDTH // view_w) // DISTMAP`, pre-flooring 320//view_w, while the docstring (lines 72-73) cites DOOM's `j*SCREENWIDTH/viewwidth/DISTMAP` (numerator-first) as the source formula. The two agree exactly when view_w divides 320 — the certified 160 config, hence every golden passes — but diverge at any non-divisor width (view_w=100, j=5: DOOM startmap-8 vs code startmap-7) and collapse to zero falloff at view_w>320 (320//640=0 kills wall distance-lighting entirely). Width is a real config axis: cfg.VIEW_W = Config.W (config.py:33), and the config explicitly designs for non-160 widths (COL_BITS "never a fixed 8", TEXTURE_DOWNSCALE's max(1, NATIVE_W//W) clamp); no constraint restricts W to divisors of 320. Sibling tables (zlight_table, yslope_table) divide numerator-first, making this the lone outlier. The proposed fix `(j * DOOM_SCREENWIDTH // view_w) // DISTMAP` is provably byte-identical at all widths dividing 320 (j*(320//w) == j*320//w when exact), so it cannot perturb the certification — a zero-risk correction of a genuine latent R6 divergence.

claim: coarse_angle_bounds' documented 'guaranteed SUPERSET' invariant does not hold against the renderer's actual angle tta[_slope_div(num,den)]: the GUARD_DEFAULT=1<<22 budget only covers tantoangle quantization, not _slope_div's block-FP truncation error, and it ignores the den<512 clamp entirely.
scenario: reference_model._slope_div (the value point_to_angle really uses) carries relative slope error ~1/256 (num truncation) + ~1/256 (3-nibble mantissa) + 255/den (den>>8); worst-case BAM deviation is ~342M*rel, i.e. ~4.0M at den=65536 (a vertex 1 map unit from the eye) — already at the 4.19M guard's edge — and it exceeds the guard for sub-map-unit deltas; for den<512 _slope_div returns SLOPERANGE so the true base is ANG45 regardless of which wedge the exact ratio picked, far outside low-wedge intervals. A viewpoint fractionally off a vertex (reachable once M14 fixed-point movement lands) would then get a wall culled as 'provably invisible' while on screen. Currently unreachable in the shipped binary — generate_coarse_bounds_fj is imported in wall_renderer.py:43 but never called and proj.coarse_bracket is never instantiated — which is exactly how it evades the 260-frame certification; the invariant must be repaired (or the near-vertex case excluded from culling) before this module is ever wired in.
v_reason: Confirmed against the code. (1) The "guaranteed SUPERSET" invariant (coarse_cull.py:12, repeated in projection.fj:214) is measured against the exact ratio wedge, but the renderer's true angle is tta[_slope_div(num,den)] (reference_model.py:363-385), and _slope_div's left-normalize branch truncates num via (num>>8)<<k (reference_model.py:343) — concrete counterexample: dx=767, dy=511 gives exact-ratio wedge 5 (interval lower bound tta[1280]-2^22 ≈ 377.6M BAM) while _slope_div(511,767)=1024 → tta[1024] ≈ 316.9M BAM, outside the interval by ~60M BAM, 14x the GUARD_DEFAULT=1<<22 budget (verified with RK=24 from tables.py:190). (2) The den<512 clamp to SLOPERANGE (base ANG45 ≈ 537M BAM) is handled by neither octant_wedge_idx (coarse_cull.py:59-74) nor the fj coarse_bracket macro (projection.fj:217-314, pure sign-folds + wedge compares, no den test), so low-wedge intervals miss it entirely. (3) Evasion of certification checks out: generate_coarse_bounds_fj is imported at wall_renderer.py:43 but has zero call sites repo-wide, and proj.coarse_bracket/frustum_sector are defined but never invoked (wall_renderer.py:519 documents the pre-pass was priced at +24.7M and dropped) — and on the certified integer vertex/viewpoint grid the truncation error stays within ~8 tantoangle indices (~2.7M BAM < guard), so only fractional positions (M14 movement) or sub-map-unit deltas expose it. Consequence is a silent visible-wall cull ("provably invisible" is false). Latent R6 defect worth fixing now: repair the guard/error model and exclude the near-vertex case, or delete the dead module, before it is ever wired in. Minor note: the reviewer's error model actually understates the worst case — num truncation alone can be ~50% relative (not ~1/256) for num just under a 256 boundary.

claim: _resolve_sprite_wad silently substitutes the map wad when an explicitly passed sprite_wad PATH exists but carries no S_START..S_END block, while the same condition on an already-loaded WadFile raises — and the docstring promises fallback only 'when that file is absent'.

The tested cases (tests/host/test_e1m1_integration.py:146-155) never cover exists-but-spriteless with a sprite-bearing map wad.

The test (tests/host/test_e1m1_integration.py:146-155) covers absent-path, spriteless-WadFile, and valid-wad cases but never exists-but-spriteless with a sprite-bearing map wad, so the silent branch is uncovered. Certification is unaffected (shipped config passes the sprite-bearing DEFAULT_SPRITE_WAD with a spriteless map fixture, never entering this branch), making this a latent contract violation for future inputs. The fix (raise or warn on exists-but-spriteless, mirroring the WadFile branch) cannot change any certified build, so it is worth doing now; hence needs_code_change=true despite design severity.

claim: scalelight_table reorders DOOM's integer division — `j * (DOOM_SCREENWIDTH // view_w) // DISTMAP` instead of DOOM's left-to-right `(j*SCREENWIDTH)//viewwidth//DISTMAP` — so the table matches the DOOM formula the docstring claims is faithfully reproduced only when view_w divides 320 exactly.
scenario: Certification evades this because VIEW_W=160 divides 320 (both orders give exactly j). Rebuild at any view width not dividing 320 — e.g. view_w=100: DOOM gives floor(3.2j)//2 while this gives floor(3j/2), several colormap rows off at high j; and any view_w>320 makes the term 0, eliminating wall light falloff entirely. Oracle and fj stay mirrored (both read this table) but both silently diverge from the documented DOOM behaviour. Fix `j * DOOM_SCREENWIDTH // view_w // DISTMAP` is byte-identical at the shipped 160.
v_reason: Verified at src/doomfj/tables.py:85 — the code computes `j * (320 // view_w) // DISTMAP`, pre-truncating 320//view_w, while its own docstring (lines 72-73) documents DOOM's left-to-right `(j*SCREENWIDTH)//viewwidth//DISTMAP`. At the shipped VIEW_W=160 both orders yield exactly j (320//160=2, 2j//2 = j), so the 7-gate and 260-frame byte-exact certifications are structurally blind to it — the evasion story holds. At view_w=100 the results diverge (j=10: 15 vs DOOM's 16, gap grows with j), and at any view_w>320 the term is 0, eliminating wall light falloff entirely. Config is explicitly a free 2-const resolution switch (config.py header bans width-assuming literals), and the docstring calls view_w "load-bearing" for exactly the non-divisor widths where the code breaks. Oracle and fj both read this one kernel, so they stay mirrored but jointly diverge from the documented DOOM behavior. The fix `j * DOOM_SCREENWIDTH // view_w // DISTMAP` is byte-identical at 160 and 320 and matches DOOM at all widths — a zero-risk latent-defect fix worth taking now.

claim: On the non-native fallback path the constructor's fully-parsed Reader memory dict (the ~350MB the docstring itself warns about for E1M1-scale images) is kept alive for the whole session, because the `self._mem.memory = {}` cleanup sits inside the `if self.native:` block while fallback `run()` re-reads the .fjm from disk and never uses the dict.

v_reason: Verified against the code: fjm_reader.Reader.__init__ eagerly builds the full word dict (_init_memory, fjm_reader.py:147-180), fastrun.py:75 clears it only inside the `if self.native:` block (line 57), and the fallback run() (fastrun.py:79-82) re-parses from disk via fj.run and never touches self._mem; grep shows no other consumer of ._mem, so on the explicitly-supported no-C-extension install (fastrun.py:34-37, 43-45) the ~350MB dict is held for the walker's whole session (walk_e1m1.py:189) while being dead weight. No certification conflict: host-side memory only, and certified runs use the native path. Fix is one safe line (clear memory unconditionally); real latent resource defect, not mere style.

claim: The fjm cache key hashes the map wad bytes and the flag tuple but omits the ASSET wad (aw) and SPRITE wad (spr) bytes/paths, even though both are baked into the emitted program — so two launches with different --asset or --sprites (or after the asset wad's contents change) collide on the same key and the second silently serves a stale binary with the wrong art.
scenario: 1) `python scripts/walk_e1m1.py --wad tests/fixtures/arena.wad --map MAP01` builds with art from assets/freedoom1.wad (the geometry-only fallback) and caches key K. 2) `python scripts/walk_e1m1.py --wad tests/fixtures/arena.wad --map MAP01 --asset tests/fixtures/freedoom_assets.wad` computes the identical K (args.asset appears nowhere in the hash at lines 143-150), prints "cache HIT", and renders every frame with the freedoom1 textures/flats/colormap while the host palette `pal = aw.playpal()` (line 193) comes from the NEW asset wad — mismatched colors on screen with no error. Same collision for any `--sprites` variation. Evades certification because the walker cache is a host-tool path the byte-exact gates never run; the certified builds all use one fixed asset config.
v_reason: The cache key at scripts/walk_e1m1.py:143-150 hashes only the fj sources, three Python files, the flag tuple, and the MAP wad bytes; the resolved asset wad (aw) and sprite wad (spr) are omitted even though emit_wall_renderer bakes both into the program (colormap/textures/flats/palette/sky/step banks from asset_wad at wall_renderer.py:264-424; the sprite bank from sprite_wad at 428-441). Launching the same map first without --asset (freedoom1 fallback, the documented geometry-only-wad path at lines 109-115) and then with --asset tests/fixtures/freedoom_assets.wad — the exact invocation the docstring advertises — yields the identical key, a "cache HIT", and a stale binary with the old art while pal=aw.playpal() (line 193) uses the new wad: silently mismatched rendering. Same collision for any --sprites change (only want_things is hashed, not which sprite wad) and for edits to a non-map wad's contents. This violates the key's own stated invariant ("pure function of (sources, flags, wad bytes)") and R6; it evades certification because the walker fjm cache is a host-tool path the byte-exact gates never run. Fix is small: hash the resolved aw and spr bytes into the key.

claim: The render-failure handler's comment says "step back and carry on" but the code never restores the pre-move (px,py) — after a crash the player position stays at the invalid viewpoint, so every subsequent move renders from a broken base and the last good position is lost.
scenario: Walk forward through an outer wall until the fj renderer raises (viewpoint outside any subsector): the exception prints, but px/py keep the out-of-map values; pressing W again moves further out and fails again, and the user must guess their way back blind because the window still shows the last good frame from a position that no longer matches the caption.
v_reason: Verified at scripts/walk_e1m1.py:276-280: px/py/ang are mutated in the KEYDOWN handlers before render() is tried, and the except arm only prints — no snapshot/rollback exists anywhere, so after a render crash the internal position stays at the invalid viewpoint while the window and caption keep the last good frame, and further moves compound from the broken base. The comment "step back and carry on" promises a restore the code never performs. One overstatement in the scenario: recovery is not truly "blind guessing" — with ang unchanged, pressing S exactly inverts each failed W (same rounding) — but the user gets no visual confirmation and inversion breaks down if they turn/strafe meanwhile. Certification is irrelevant cover: the byte-exact gates and 260-frame sweep never run this host-side interactive event loop. A real (if minor, design-severity) defect in the owner's primary play tool; the fix is a trivial pre-move snapshot restored in the except arm.
